tool.name: EulerDeconvolution
tool.summary: Euler deconvolution: estimates the position and depth of gravity or magnetic sources from the grid's gradients in moving windows, keeping the most reliable solutions (Reliable Euler Deconvolution, Melo & Barbosa 2020).
tool.usage:
The same solver as the QGIS plugin.

The output CSV has one row per kept solution: X, Y, Depth, B (base level) and StdDfDz (the standard deviation of the vertical derivative in the window, used to rank them).

param.name: in_raster
param.dialogReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).
param.pythonReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).

param.name: si
param.dialogReference: Structural index: 0 contact, 1 dyke or sill edge, 2 pipe or horizontal cylinder, 3 sphere or dipole.
param.pythonReference: Structural index: 0 contact, 1 dyke or sill edge, 2 pipe or horizontal cylinder, 3 sphere or dipole.

param.name: window_size
param.dialogReference: Width of the moving window in pixels (odd).
param.pythonReference: Width of the moving window in pixels (odd).

param.name: threshold
param.dialogReference: Fraction of the solutions to keep (0-1), those with the largest standard deviation of the vertical derivative: 0.1 keeps the best 10%.
param.pythonReference: Fraction of the solutions to keep (0-1), those with the largest standard deviation of the vertical derivative: 0.1 keeps the best 10%.
